subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should trusted plugins receive a public agent-scoped keyed-store API, or should plugin state remain in the shared plugin-owned store with agent identity encoded inside the plugin namespace?
rationale: Both models are technically viable, but they create different cross-agent authorization, lifecycle, backup, and third-party compatibility contracts that repository evidence cannot choose safely.

options.title: Add a narrow agent store
options.body: Extend `api.runtime.state` with an explicit agent-bound store available only after host validation of the plugin and target agent.

options.title: Keep shared plugin storage
options.body: Retain `openKeyedStore` as the canonical store and require plugins to include agent identity in their namespace or keys when needed.

options.title: Expose a general cache
options.body: Add the proposed generic cache facade for external plugins, accepting a broader public API and security surface.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow agent store
recommendation.body: Extend `api.runtime.state` with an explicit agent-bound store available only after host validation of the plugin and target agent.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to defining and maintaining the public Plugin SDK boundary.
